Subject: MSA redlines + operator credentialing approach

Diego,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are our latest MSA redlines (MediArc_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) and a short diagram of the topology we're concerned about (key-handback-diagram.pdf). Two items drive these asks: (1) we must ensure operator access into our VPC/on-prem clusters is strictly bounded and auditable, and (2) board-level guidance requires an "escrow-lite" capability for operator credentials and access evidence in case of prolonged service interruption.

High-level asks:
- An addendum that clarifies license scope for private deployments and that operator credentials are limited to temporary, auditable operator sessions;
- A mechanism to provide a sealed, encrypted snapshot of operator credentials (no plaintext keys) and an attestation signed by a third-party auditor on a quarterly basis or on demand after an incident;
- Commitment to provide log exports and Operator Access Attestations within 10 business days following a verified incident;
- Clear boundaries that this is not a source-code escrow but an evidence/credential handback process.

Please let me know if Redwood has a standard addendum template for this or if you prefer to propose language. We're trying to keep review cycles short; if possible we'd like a Redwood proposal this week so our counsel can mark it up.

Thanks,
Jacob
Contracts Manager
MediArc Health
(contracts@medi-arc.com)

Jacob / Diego — putting our initial position on paper to speed things along. Below are points we'd put in an addendum; this is Redwood's proposed framing for review by MediArc counsel.

Proposed: "Operator Credentialing & Evidence Addendum (OC&E Addendum)" — summary bullets:
- Scope: Applies only to private deployments explicitly identified in the Order Form (VPC instances and listed on-prem sites). This is not a general grant of deployment rights beyond those Order Form locations.
- Credential custody: Redwood will produce encrypted KMS snapshots (AES-256-GCM) for operator credentials, encrypted using the customer's supplied RSA-4096 public key. Redwood retains control of its private operational keys; snapshots are encrypted client-side for handback only.
- Escrow-lite flow: On a quarterly cadence and upon validated incident request, Redwood will upload the encrypted snapshot to a mutually agreed SFTP or a sealed third-party escrow agent. Each snapshot will be accompanied by a signed attestation from Redwood and, where requested, a third-party auditor (if MediArc engages one).
- Operator sessions: Operator access will be time-limited, approved via documented maintenance windows, and require multi-factor admin authorization. Temporary operator keys expire automatically after the window. All operator sessions are logged and retained per the retention table in the SOW.
- Evidence: Redwood commits to delivering Operator Access Attestations and relevant log exports within 10 business days of a validated incident. For high-sensitivity incidents Redwood will prioritize with a 5-business-day SLA subject to scope.
- Limitations: No transfer of source code or intellectual property. This addendum does not broaden license to include derivative rights; it is narrowly tailored to evidence/credential handback and attestation.

We attach a draft addendum (proposed-addendum-redwood.docx) with tracked language. Two items we'd like MediArc to confirm before we finalize: (a) receiving party for the snapshots (SFTP vs named escrow agent), and (b) whether MediArc will engage an independent auditor or prefer Redwood to source a mutually acceptable auditor and bill pass-through costs.

If that aligns, we can produce a redline directly against your attached MSA document and push to you via DocuSign for a quick cycle.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30–60 minute call to work through any language.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel, Product
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Diego — thanks, that framing mostly aligns with our expectations and helps narrow the review. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

1) Receiving party: MediArc prefers snapshots land on a named escrow agent (we will provide the agent's details). If Redwood insists on SFTP, the agent requires write-only credentials and signed transfer logs.
2) Auditor: MediArc will engage an independent third-party auditor; we'd like Redwood to accept the auditor's role and cooperate (Redwood's cooperation will be narrowly scoped to signature/verification of the uploaded snapshot).
3) Evidence SLA: please confirm the 10-business-day standard for non-high-sensitivity incidents and the 5-business-day priority SLA will be added as an optional accelerated path in the addendum. Counsel also asked for explicit language that attestations include a minimally structured CSV of operator session start/stop times and session purpose.

We attached a marked-up copy of the MSA redlines (redlines_marked.pdf). If you can accept the escrow agent approach and the structured attestation format, we can move to DocuSign.
